---
description: "How complete and accurate Island Transit's live bus tracking is: trips seen, gaps, location age and prediction misses."
title: "Can the data be trusted?"
subtitle: "How reliable Island Transit's bus-tracking feed is, checked every day"
---

Trip-planning apps, this site, and anyone else who studies Island Transit
all lean on the same live feed, so every number built on it is only as good
as the feed itself. That's why we grade the feed every day.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
import {csv, json, pct, num, count, routeLabel, longDate, isoDate, serviceDays, SERIES, DATA_URL} from "./lib.js"
daily = csv(d3, "data/quality/daily.csv")
// Days with scheduled service; a holiday is archived and listed under "All
// days" but not graded or charted.
days = serviceDays(daily).map(d => ({...d, prediction_min_5min: d.prediction_median_abs_s_5min == null ? null : d.prediction_median_abs_s_5min / 60,
  day: isoDate(d.service_date), date: new Date(`${isoDate(d.service_date)}T12:00:00Z`)}))
latestDate = days.length ? days.at(-1).day : null
latest = latestDate ? json(`data/quality/days/${latestDate}.json`) : null
noData = () => days.length === 0
  ? html`<p class="empty">No day has been processed yet.</p>`
  : html`<p class="empty">The details for ${longDate(latestDate)} can't be shown right now.</p>`
// Charts are drawn at the width of their column, so text keeps its size on a phone.
half = width < 768 ? width : Math.floor((width - 24) / 2)
clock = iso => new Date(iso).toLocaleTimeString("en-US", {hour: "numeric", minute: "2-digit", timeZone: "America/Los_Angeles"})
partial = latest?.scheduled_service?.trips_ended_before_collection > 0
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
lq = days.at(-1) ?? null
html`${lq == null ? noData() : html`<p class="note">These grades are for ${longDate(latestDate)}.${partial ? ` Collection began at ${clock(latest.paradata.observed_from)} Pacific that day, so the grades cover only part of it.` : ""}</p>
<div class="stat-row">
  <div class="stat"><div class="label">Did every scheduled trip show up?</div>
    <div class="value">${pct(lq.trip_coverage)}</div>
    <div class="note">of ${count(lq.scheduled_trips)} scheduled trips appeared in the tracking around the time they were due</div></div>
  <div class="stat"><div class="label">Did the collector keep running?</div>
    <div class="value">${pct(lq.vehicle_uptime, 1)}</div>
    <div class="note">of 20-second checks got a good answer from the feed</div></div>
  <div class="stat"><div class="label">How fresh are bus locations?</div>
    <div class="value">${num(lq.position_age_s_median)} seconds</div>
    <div class="note">typical age of a location when it first appears</div></div>
  <div class="stat"><div class="label">How close are arrival predictions?</div>
    <div class="value">${lq.prediction_min_5min == null ? "–" : `${num(lq.prediction_min_5min, 1)} min`}</div>
    <div class="note">typical miss, for predictions made 5 minutes before the bus arrived${lq.prediction_over_30min_share_5min ? `; ${pct(lq.prediction_over_30min_share_5min, 0)} were off by more than 30 minutes` : ""}</div></div>
  <div class="stat"><div class="label">Are buses where the route says?</div>
    <div class="value">${pct(1 - lq.off_shape_share)}</div>
    <div class="note">of locations were within 100 meters (about 330 feet) of the bus's published route</div></div>
</div>`}`
```

We sort the details below the way survey researchers grade any source of
data, into [coverage]{.term tabindex="0" tip="Coverage asks whether every scheduled trip shows up in the tracking at all."},
[nonresponse]{.term tabindex="0" tip="Nonresponse is data that should be there but is missing, such as a failed request, an empty feed, or a gap in a bus's reports."},
[measurement error]{.term tabindex="0" tip="Measurement error is data that is there but wrong, such as GPS wobble, a bus that seems to jump, an old location, or a prediction that misses."},
[processing error]{.term tabindex="0" tip="A processing error happens when data can't be matched up, such as a trip in the feed that isn't in the schedule."}
and [paradata]{.term tabindex="0" tip="Paradata is data about the collection itself: every request the collector made, how long it took, and whether it worked."}.
Hover over or tap each term for a plain explanation, or see the
[Methods](methods.qmd) page for the exact definitions.

## Over time

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
series = [
  {key: "trip_coverage", title: "Scheduled trips seen in the feed", unit: "share"},
  {key: "vehicle_uptime", title: "Collector uptime (vehicle locations)", unit: "share"},
  {key: "stale_in_service_rate", title: "Feed more than 2 minutes behind during service", unit: "share"},
  {key: "position_age_s_median", title: "Typical age of a bus location when first seen (seconds)", unit: "s"},
  {key: "longest_gap_s_median", title: "Typical longest tracking gap per trip (seconds)", unit: "s"},
  {key: "timepoint_coverage", title: "Departures at timetable stops we could time", unit: "share"},
  {key: "prediction_min_5min", title: "Typical arrival prediction miss, 5 minutes ahead (minutes)", unit: "min"},
]
shown = (s, d) => s.unit === "share" ? pct(d[s.key], 1) : `${num(d[s.key], 1)} ${s.unit === "min" ? "minutes" : "seconds"}`
html`${days.length === 0 ? noData() : days.length < 2 ? html`<p class="empty">Charts that follow each measure over time will appear once there is a second day of data.</p>` : html`<div class="grid">${series.map(s => html`<div class="g-col-12 g-col-md-6">
  <h3 class="chart-title">${s.title}</h3>
  ${Plot.plot({
    ariaLabel: `${s.title}, by service day`,
    ariaDescription: `From ${longDate(days[0].day)} to ${longDate(latestDate)}. Latest value: ${shown(s, days.at(-1))}.`,
    style: {background: "transparent"},
    width: half, height: 200, marginLeft: 50, marginRight: 30,
    x: {type: "utc", label: null, ticks: days.length <= 5 ? days.map(d => d.date) : 5, tickFormat: "%b %-d"},
    y: {grid: true, label: null, tickFormat: s.unit === "share" ? (d => `${Math.round(d * 100)}%`) : undefined,
        domain: s.unit === "share" ? [0, 1] : undefined},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleY([0]),
      Plot.lineY(days, {x: "date", y: s.key, stroke: SERIES, strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.dot(days, {x: "date", y: s.key, fill: SERIES, r: 4}),
      Plot.tip(days, Plot.pointerX({x: "date", y: s.key,
        title: d => `${longDate(d.day)}\n${shown(s, d)}`})),
    ],
  })}</div>`)}</div>`}`
```

## Details

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`${latest == null ? noData() : html`<p>These details are for ${longDate(latestDate)}, measured against Passio schedule version
  <code>${latest.schedule.passio_version}</code>.</p>`}`
```

<details class="more"><summary>Trip coverage by route</summary>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
byRoute = latest == null ? [] : Object.entries(latest.coverage.by_route).map(([id, c]) => ({
  route: routeLabel(latest.routes, id), ...c}))
html`${byRoute.length === 0 ? noData() : Plot.plot({
  ariaLabel: `Share of scheduled trips seen in the tracking, by route, ${longDate(latestDate)}`,
  ariaDescription: byRoute.map(d => `${d.route}: ${pct(d.coverage)}`).join("; "),
  style: {background: "transparent"},
  width: Math.max(320, Math.min(width, 960)), marginLeft: width < 640 ? 150 : 260, height: 28 * byRoute.length + 40,
  x: {domain: [0, 1], grid: true, label: "Share of scheduled trips seen", tickFormat: d => `${Math.round(d * 100)}%`},
  y: {label: null},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(byRoute, {y: "route", x: "coverage", fill: SERIES, rx: 2, sort: {y: "x", reverse: true}}),
    Plot.ruleX([0]),
    Plot.tip(byRoute, Plot.pointerY({y: "route", x: "coverage",
      title: d => `${d.route}\n${d.observed} of ${d.scheduled} trips (${pct(d.coverage)})`})),
  ],
})}`
```

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>Timepoint events observed, by route</summary>

This shows how many scheduled departures at printed timepoints (or arrivals,
at a trip's last stop) we could put a time on, using the bus locations.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
ev = latest?.events ?? null
stopRoute = ev == null ? [] : Object.entries(ev.stop_coverage.timepoints.by_route).map(([id, c]) => ({
  route: routeLabel(latest.routes, id), ...c,
  off_shape_share: ev.shape_fit.by_route[id]?.off_shape_share ?? null}))
html`${stopRoute.length === 0 ? noData() : Plot.plot({
  ariaLabel: `Share of scheduled timepoint events we could time, by route, ${longDate(latestDate)}`,
  ariaDescription: stopRoute.map(d => `${d.route}: ${pct(d.coverage)}`).join("; "),
  style: {background: "transparent"},
  width: Math.max(320, Math.min(width, 960)), marginLeft: width < 640 ? 150 : 260, height: 28 * stopRoute.length + 40,
  x: {domain: [0, 1], grid: true, label: "Share of scheduled timepoint events observed", tickFormat: d => `${Math.round(d * 100)}%`},
  y: {label: null},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(stopRoute, {y: "route", x: "coverage", fill: SERIES, rx: 2, sort: {y: "x", reverse: true}}),
    Plot.ruleX([0]),
    Plot.tip(stopRoute, Plot.pointerY({y: "route", x: "coverage",
      title: d => `${d.route}\n${d.observed} of ${d.scheduled} events (${pct(d.coverage)})\nPositions off the route shape: ${pct(d.off_shape_share, 1)}`})),
  ],
})}`
```

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>Arrival predictions</summary>

For each prediction, we take the arrival time the feed was showing a given
number of minutes ahead and subtract the arrival time we estimated from the
bus's locations. A positive error means the bus showed up earlier than the
feed said it would. Some predictions carry the wrong day's date, so we count
those separately and leave them out of the error figures. A few others are
off by hours, which pulls the mean far from the typical miss, so the table
gives both the mean and the median and counts the predictions that were off
by more than 30 minutes.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
pred = ev == null ? [] : Object.entries(ev.prediction_error.by_horizon_min).map(([h, b]) => ({
  "Minutes ahead": +h, "Predictions": b.n, "Mean error (s)": b.bias_s, "Median error (s)": b.median_s,
  "Typical miss (s)": b.median_abs_s, "Mean miss (s)": b.mae_s, "Within 60 s": b.within_60s_share,
  "Off by over 30 min": b.over_30min, "Dated another day": b.other_day}))
html`${pred.length === 0 ? noData() : Inputs.table(pred, {select: false, format: {"Within 60 s": d => pct(d, 1)}, rows: 10})}`
```

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>Fields the feed leaves empty</summary>

This table shows how often each field is missing from the position reports.
When a field is missing from every single report, the feed simply doesn't
send it.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
items = latest == null ? [] : Object.entries(latest.nonresponse.items.missing_share)
  .map(([field, share]) => ({field, share}))
html`${items.length === 0 ? noData() : Inputs.table(items, {select: false,
  columns: ["field", "share"], header: {field: "Field", share: "Missing"},
  format: {share: d => pct(d, 1)}, rows: 25})}`
```

</details>

  ["Trip ids found in the schedule", pct(latest.processing.id_match.trip_id.match_rate, 1)],
  ["Stop ids found in the schedule", pct(latest.processing.id_match.stop_id.match_rate, 1)],
  ["Median response time, vehicle positions", `${num(latest.paradata.vehiclePositions.latency_ms_median)} ms`],
  ...(latest.paradata.tripUpdates.refresh == null ? [] : [
    ["Checks 20 seconds apart in which a trip's prediction had changed", pct(latest.paradata.tripUpdates.refresh.changed_share, 1)],
    ["Typical time between new predictions for a trip", `${num(latest.paradata.tripUpdates.refresh.update_interval_s_median)} seconds`],
  ]),
  ["Distinct vehicles reporting", latest.coverage.vehicles_seen],
  ...(ev == null ? [] : [
    ["All stop events with an inferred time", pct(ev.stop_coverage.all_stops.coverage, 1)],
    ["Positions more than 100 meters (330 ft) off the route shape", pct(ev.shape_fit.off_shape_share, 1)],
    ["Positions moving against the route shape", pct(ev.shape_fit.wrong_direction_share, 1)],
    ["Trips that left out part of the published route shape", `${ev.shape_fit.trips_skipping_part_of_shape} (${num(ev.shape_fit.skipped_km, 1)} km)`],
    ["Route shapes that draw segments three times (corrected)", `${ev.retraced_shapes.shapes_retraced} of ${ev.retraced_shapes.shapes_used}`],
    ["Trip ids seen that are not scheduled that day", `${ev.assignment.unassignable} of ${ev.assignment.observed_trip_ids}`],
    ["Position jitter at terminals, 95th percentile", `${num(ev.jitter.jitter_m_p95, 1)} meters`],
    ["Vehicles seen in the previous 30 days but not this day",
      ev.missing_vehicles.missing_count == null ? "no earlier days" : ev.missing_vehicles.missing_count],
  ]),
].map(([measure, value]) => ({measure, value}))
html`${other.length === 0 ? noData() : Inputs.table(other, {select: false, header: {measure: "Measure", value: "Value"}, rows: 30})}`

<details class="more"><summary>Randomness of gaps</summary>

When the feed misses a trip, is that bad luck spread evenly, or does it
tend to happen at certain hours, on certain routes, or when lots of buses
are out at once? The tables below show the share of scheduled trips that
sent no position report around the time they were due, over every day so
far. Once there are
14 days and 30 missed trips, a statistical model called a logistic
regression will test all of these at the same time.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
gaps = json("data/quality/gaps.json")
pval = p => p == null ? "–" : p < 0.0001 ? "< 0.0001" : `= ${num(p, 4)}`
gapTables = gaps == null || gaps.rates == null ? [] : [
  ["Hour band (Pacific)", gaps.rates.by_hour_band],
  ["Trips in service at the trip's start", gaps.rates.by_trips_in_service],
  ["Day type", gaps.rates.by_day_type],
  ["Route", Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(gaps.rates.by_route)
    .map(([id, v]) => [routeLabel(latest && latest.routes, id), v]))],
]
html`${gapTables.length === 0 ? noData() : html`
  <p>Over ${gaps.days.length} day${gaps.days.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}, ${count(gaps.trips)} trips were scheduled and
    ${count(gaps.unobserved)} sent no position report within 30 minutes of their scheduled time.</p>
  <div class="grid">${gapTables.map(([title, t]) => html`<div class="g-col-12 g-col-md-6">
    <h3 class="chart-title">${title}</h3>
    ${Inputs.table(Object.entries(t).map(([group, v]) => ({group, ...v})), {select: false,
      columns: ["group", "scheduled", "unobserved", "rate"],
      header: {group: "", scheduled: "Scheduled", unobserved: "Not seen", rate: "Share not seen"},
      format: {scheduled: count, unobserved: count, rate: d => pct(d, 1)}, rows: 20, layout: "auto"})}</div>`)}</div>`}`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
html`${gaps == null ? "" : gaps.model == null ? html`<p><em>${gaps.model_status.startsWith("not fitted: needs") ? `The model hasn't been fitted yet, because it ${gaps.model_status.slice("not fitted: ".length)}.` : `Model status: ${gaps.model_status}.`}</em></p>` : html`
  <p>This logistic regression looks at ${gaps.model.trips} trips and asks which ones the feed missed. We fit it with
  Firth's penalized likelihood, which keeps the estimates sensible even when a route never missed a trip.
  Testing all the predictors together gives χ² = ${num(gaps.model.lr_test_all_predictors.statistic, 1)},
  df = ${gaps.model.lr_test_all_predictors.df}, p ${pval(gaps.model.lr_test_all_predictors.p)}.
  A small p-value means the gaps are not missing completely at random, so something about the hour, the route,
  the day or the number of buses out is tied to which trips go missing. The model treats every trip as
  separate, but trips lost on the same day or the same bus tend to go missing together, so the p-values
  here are more confident than they should be. Each odds ratio compares a group with
  ${gaps.model.reference_levels["hour band"]}, route ${routeLabel(latest && latest.routes, gaps.model.reference_levels.route)}
  and ${gaps.model.reference_levels["day type"]}.${gaps.model.converged ? "" : " The model did not settle on a stable answer (it did not converge), so treat these numbers with caution."}</p>
  ${Inputs.table(gaps.model.terms.filter(t => t.term !== "intercept").map(t => ({...t,
      term: t.term.startsWith("route: ") ? `route: ${routeLabel(latest && latest.routes, t.term.slice(7))}` : t.term,
      ci: `${num(t.or_95ci[0], 2)} to ${num(t.or_95ci[1], 2)}`})), {select: false,
    columns: ["term", "odds_ratio", "ci", "p"],
    header: {term: "Term", odds_ratio: "Odds ratio", ci: "95% interval", p: "p"},
    format: {odds_ratio: d => num(d, 2), p: d => pval(d).replace(/^= /, "")}, rows: 30})}`}`
```

The model and the data behind it are in
[`quality/gaps.json`](https://github.com/dfladagermccullugh-bot/Open-Island-Transit-Data/blob/data/quality/gaps.json).
Holidays on which Island Transit runs no buses are left out.

</details>

<details class="more"><summary>All days</summary>

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
allDays = daily.map(d => ({day: isoDate(d.service_date), service: d.service_expected === false ? "No service (holiday)" : "Yes",
  trips: d.scheduled_trips, coverage: d.trip_coverage, uptime: d.vehicle_uptime, age: d.position_age_s_median,
  timed: d.timepoint_coverage, off: d.off_shape_share, predict: d.prediction_median_abs_s_5min == null ? null : d.prediction_median_abs_s_5min / 60})).reverse()
html`${allDays.length === 0 ? noData() : Inputs.table(allDays, {select: false,
  header: {day: "Service day", service: "Buses scheduled", trips: "Scheduled trips", coverage: "Trips seen", uptime: "Collector uptime",
           age: "Location age (s)", timed: "Timepoint events timed", off: "Locations off route", predict: "Typical prediction miss, 5 min ahead (min)"},
  format: {day: d => longDate(d), trips: count, coverage: d => pct(d, 1), uptime: d => pct(d, 2), age: d => num(d, 1),
           timed: d => pct(d, 1), off: d => pct(d, 1), predict: d => num(d, 1)},
  rows: 15, layout: "auto"})}`
```

The file has every column, including the version of the code behind each
day. You can download it as
[`quality/daily.csv`](https://github.com/dfladagermccullugh-bot/Open-Island-Transit-Data/blob/data/quality/daily.csv).

</details>
